item.title: “Monks, with unguarded faculties, with deficiency in guarding the faculties, virtue is destroyed. With no virtue, with deficiency in virtue, right concentration is destroyed. With…
item.description:
“Monks, with unguarded faculties, with deficiency in guarding the faculties, virtue is destroyed. With no virtue, with deficiency in virtue, right concentration is destroyed. With no right concentration, with deficiency in right concentration, true knowledge and vision are destroyed. With no true knowledge and vision, with deficiency in true knowledge and vision, disenchantment and dispassion are destroyed. With no disenchantment and dispassion, with deficiency in disenchantment and dispassion, the knowledge and vision of liberation are destroyed. Just as, monks, a tree with deficient branches and foliage — its shoots do not reach perfection, its bark does not reach perfection, its sapwood does not reach perfection, its heartwood does not reach perfection. So too, monks, with unguarded faculties, with deficiency in guarding the faculties … the knowledge and vision of liberation are destroyed.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.50

item.title: “Fletchers make arrows, Potters make pots, Carpenters shape wood, The wise tame themselves.” “Like a solid rock Unmoved by the wind, So the wise are…
item.description:
“Fletchers make arrows,
Potters make pots,
Carpenters shape wood,
The wise tame themselves.”

“Like a solid rock
Unmoved by the wind,
So the wise are unmoved
Amid praise and blame.”

“Like a deep lake,
Clear, unruffled,
So the wise become serene,
Hearing the Dhamma.”

“The good renounce everything,
The virtuous do not prattle about sensual desires.
Whether touched by pleasure or pain,
The wise show neither elation nor depression.”

From: Dhammapada 76-89

item.title: “And what, monks, is the origin of suffering? Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is contact. With contact…
item.description:
“And what, monks, is the origin of suffering? Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is contact. With contact as condition, feeling. With feeling as condition, craving. This is the origin of suffering. Dependent on the ear … on the nose … on the tongue … on the body … Dependent on the mind and phenomena, mind-consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is contact. With contact as condition, feeling. With feeling as condition, craving. This, monks, is the origin of suffering.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.106
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “There is, monks, an unborn, unbecome, unmade, unconditioned. If there were not that unborn, unbecome, unmade, unconditioned, no escape would be discerned from the born,…
item.description:
“There is, monks, an unborn, unbecome, unmade, unconditioned. If there were not that unborn, unbecome, unmade, unconditioned, no escape would be discerned from the born, become, made, conditioned. But because there is an unborn, unbecome, unmade, unconditioned, therefore escape is discerned from the born, become, made, conditioned.”

That which is born, become, arisen,
Made, conditioned, impermanent,
Composed of aging and death,
A nest of disease, perishable,
Born from nutriment and craving —
That is not fit to delight in.

But the escape from that —
Peace, beyond reasoning,
Unborn, unbecome,
The sorrowless state, the path without defilement,
The cessation of painful states,
The stilling of conditioned things —
That is happiness.

From: Itivuttaka 43

item.title: “Monks, those ascetics or brahmins in the past … in the future … in the present who regard whatever in the world is agreeable and…
item.description:
“Monks, those ascetics or brahmins in the past … in the future … in the present who regard whatever in the world is agreeable and enticing as permanent, as happiness, as healthy, as safe, as self — they increase craving. Those who increase craving, increase attachment. Those who increase attachment, increase suffering. Those who increase suffering are not freed from birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. I say that they are not freed from suffering.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 12.66
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Udāyi, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye—desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. Sounds cognizable…
item.description:
“Udāyi, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye—desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. Sounds cognizable by the ear … Odors cognizable by the nose … Tastes cognizable by the tongue … Tangibles cognizable by the body—desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. These, Udāyi, are the five strands of sensual pleasure. Whatever pleasure or joy arises in dependence on these five strands of sensual pleasure, that is called sensual pleasure, defiled pleasure, worldling’s pleasure, ignoble pleasure. I say that such pleasure should not be pursued, should not be developed, should not be cultivated, should be feared.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 66 – Laṭukikopamasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Elder Mahākāla: One who does not know thus, Yet still creates attachments — The fool goes on, Experiencing suffering again and again. Therefore, one who…
item.description:
Elder Mahākāla:

One who does not know thus,
Yet still creates attachments —
The fool goes on,
Experiencing suffering again and again.
Therefore, one who knows
Does not create attachments.
I will not lie down
With my head broken.

From: Theragāthā 2.16
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “And how, monks, is there restraint? Here, monks, when a monk sees a form with the eye, he is not attached to agreeable forms nor…
item.description:
“And how, monks, is there restraint? Here, monks, when a monk sees a form with the eye, he is not attached to agreeable forms nor repelled by disagreeable forms. He dwells with bodily mindfulness established, with an immeasurable mind. He knows as it actually is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom. Here, evil, unwholesome states that have arisen are abandoned without remainder. When he tastes a flavor … When he cognizes a phenomenon with the mind, he is not attached to agreeable phenomena nor repelled by disagreeable phenomena. He dwells with bodily mindfulness established, with an immeasurable mind. He knows as it actually is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom. Here, evil, unwholesome states that have arisen are abandoned without remainder. Thus, monks, is restraint.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.244
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, if a monk lives without ardor in his practice, though he may wish: ‘May my mind be liberated from the defilements without clinging,’ yet…
item.description:
“Monks, if a monk lives without ardor in his practice, though he may wish: ‘May my mind be liberated from the defilements without clinging,’ yet his mind is not liberated from the defilements without clinging. Why is that? It is because he has not developed. Not developed what? He has not developed the four foundations of mindfulness. He has not developed the four right efforts. He has not developed the four bases of spiritual power. He has not developed the five faculties. He has not developed the five powers. He has not developed the seven factors of enlightenment. He has not developed the Noble Eightfold Path.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.101
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Elder Eraka: “O Eraka, painful are sensual pleasures! O Eraka, not happiness are sensual pleasures! One who desires sensual pleasures, desires suffering. One who does…
item.description:
Elder Eraka:
“O Eraka, painful are sensual pleasures!
O Eraka, not happiness are sensual pleasures!
One who desires sensual pleasures, desires suffering.
One who does not desire sensual pleasures, does not desire suffering.
O Eraka, know this as it is.”

From: Theragāthā 1.93
